notes: Consensus of coders A and B over the two included university-layer CFE documents (no school or computing-unit policy found; course layer deferred). Student guidelines KB 3406 were inaccessible (login). Samples in the policy-examples document are templates for instructors, so unit stances describe each sample, not a campus-wide rule. Boilerplate sentences repeated across the samples (talk to me, consequences wording, class discussion) are coded once, at first occurrence. Dropped one A-only unit (grammar/spell-check list item). Coder notes (fit_note, uncovered_note) from both coders were kept and merged.

documents.title: AI Teaching and Research Guidance
documents.summary: Short CFE page stating OU's approach to AI in teaching and research, pointing faculty to a Canvas course, consultations and AI literacy frameworks. It sets no rule on student AI use.
documents.stance_why: The page says 'OU does not mandate a single approach to AI in the classroom' and that faculty make discipline-appropriate choices and communicate them, so the decision is handed to instructors and the document sets no stance of its own.

units.why: The opening sentence frames AI as raising "important questions about learning goals, assessment, authorship, and academic integrity" but sets no rule; no type captures a bare framing of issues, so it is UNCOVERED rather than stretched.
units.anchor: AI raises important questions about learning goals, assessment, authorship, and academic integrity.
units.uncovered_note: Names the issues AI raises (learning goals, assessment, authorship, integrity) as context for instructor choices, without a rule.
units.resolution_why: Coders disagreed (policy_type: A=P56, B=UNCOVERED, final=UNCOVERED). A coded P56 with a fit note, B coded UNCOVERED. The sentence only names concerns AI raises and sets no framework, purpose or scope, so P56 would be a stretch; UNCOVERED kept (codebook prefers UNCOVERED over a stretched fit).

units.why: The sentence says "OU does not mandate a single approach to AI in the classroom," so the university sets no campus-wide rule and leaves the choice to instructors; that is the instructor-decides type (P04), stated as a fact.
units.anchor: OU does not mandate a single approach to AI in the classroom.
units.resolution_why: Coders disagreed (actor: A=instructor, B=admin, final=admin; phase: A=before-course, B=general, final=general). Source: 'OU does not mandate a single approach to AI in the classroom' is the university's own statement, so actor admin and phase general (B) fit better than instructor/before-course (A). Modality informs and type P04 agreed.

units.why: Faculty are 'encouraged to make intentional, discipline-appropriate choices', placing the decision with instructors and discipline; phrased as encouragement so modality is should.
units.anchor: faculty are encouraged to make intentional, discipline-appropriate choices
